clue.text: South American power with a town of insufficient space?

parts.note: the Inca were the South American people of the Andean empire
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a Peruvian, his power and a crowded town leave no room to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: read as IN-CAPACITY, the word suggests something not fitting the space available.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking capacity means being unable to hold enough, a whimsical reading of a word that normally means inability.

clue.text: Press team?

parts.note: read as a charade: to press clothes is to iron them, and a team is a side; the whole names a famous nickname and TV detective

explanation.walkthrough: Press suggests journalists, but here it means smoothing clothes with an iron; a team is a side. Ironside was Cromwell's nickname and his troopers were the Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Linking the two everyday synonyms for press and team spells out the name, so the clue is a whimsical description rather than a definition.

clue.text: Musical patroness Alice moves around Channel Islands

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes around the islands' abbreviation, holding it inside
the letters of the name Alice move about into a new order

parts.note: CI is the usual abbreviation for the Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey among them

explanation.surface: A woman called Alice, devoted to music, travels around Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice looks like the patroness herself, but her name is only fodder; Channel Islands is abbreviated, as crossword convention allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Cecilia is the patron saint of music, so she is the patroness of musicians.

clue.text: Don't take my advice, arrange espousal freely

indicators.note: arrange tells us to put the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a friend's wedding plans: forget my advice, organise the marriage however you like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' looks like it describes how to arrange, but it is part of the fodder: 'arrange' shuffles ESPOUSAL plus FREELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to do as they wish is a way of saying you won't press your advice on them.

clue.text: Get on? Quite the reverse!

parts.note: the opposite of getting on a bus is coming off it, and the exclamation of disbelief 'get on!' means much the same as this phrase

explanation.walkthrough: Get on suggests boarding, whose reverse is coming off; yet as an exclamation 'Get on (with you)!' is a scoffing retort, which is just what the answer is too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive retorts telling a speaker their claim is nonsense, while literally being opposite movements on and off a vehicle.

clue.text: Brief intersection?

annotationWithheld.why: Brief intersection? (5): TERSE sits inside 'intersection', but no clue word signals the hidden word, and as a cryptic definition the clue would spell its own answer; the check refuses both

clue.text: Objections about a short piece

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for objections is read backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone raises objections about a brief passage of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but here means turned round: BUTS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftover end of a cigarette or pencil, or the counterfoil of a ticket, is a short remaining piece.

clue.text: Sailed against the wind, keeping right, when followed

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the sailing word holds the letter for right

parts.note: to tack is to sail a zigzag course into the wind

explanation.surface: A yacht beat into the wind, holding to starboard, as another boat came after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow their trail, so tracked means pursued or followed.

clue.text: Scottish island has a name for gas

indicators.note: has means the island holds the next letters within it

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish island has its own name for a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' works as a container: BUTE holds A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: This hydrocarbon is a fuel gas sold in canisters for camping stoves and lighters.

clue.text: No bodily feature of Red Russians?

definitions.text: No bodily feature of Red Russians?

parts.words: No bodily feature of Red Russians?
parts.note: the Reds and Whites were the opposing sides of the Russian Civil War; a Red, so the joke goes, would not carry anything White in his blood

explanation.walkthrough: The Bolshevik Reds fought the anti-communist Whites, so a loyal Red would hardly have a White part in his body; the answer is in fact a part of everyone's blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A leucocyte is an immune cell in everyone's blood; the clue jokes that a Red revolutionary could not have one because of its colour.

clue.text: Copper enters unit at right time

indicators.note: enters means the copper symbol goes inside the word for unit

parts.note: one is the single unit
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman arrives at his squad exactly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer but is the metal, Cu, which goes inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor comes in at the agreed signal, so the phrase means exactly when expected.

clue.text: Troop movement on April 1 st?

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial parade of soldiers passing a saluting point
on the first day of April the previous month is over, and the phrase reads as that month having gone by

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: by the first of April, March is past.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade in which troops file by a reviewing officer; and literally, the third month has gone by once April begins.

clue.text: Primate's copy

definitions.meaning: primate is, a monkey or similar animal, with the 's as 'is' joining the two halves
to copy someone is to mimic or imitate them

explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla or chimpanzee is a primate, and mimicking someone's actions is the verb sense.

clue.text: Acts as shopkeeper in prisons, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for prisons is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: cells are rooms where prisoners are locked up

explanation.surface: A trader runs his shop from inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper's job is trading goods for money, which is what someone who vends does.

clue.text: Plain man's following one -having been this?

indicators.note: following says the man's name comes after the letter for one

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
a means one, as in 'a single'
Ken is a man's name; the 's is 'is' joining it to the indicator

explanation.surface: A man on a plain is following someone, wondering whether he has just been passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue itself: whoever is following one has been passed by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being passed on the road by a faster vehicle or runner is what the definition, read with the rest of the clue, describes.

clue.text: Ghostly record of Grossmiths?

parts.note: a ghost has no body, so its journal would be the log of one with no body; George and Weedon Grossmith wrote the comic novel of that title

explanation.walkthrough: George and Weedon Grossmith's 1892 comic novel follows the self-important clerk Charles Pooter; the clue reads its title as the journal of a ghost, one with no body.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Grossmith brothers' novel, reinterpreted as the daily journal of a bodiless spirit.

clue.text: One reduced to RR?

parts.note: the three Rs of schooling are reading, writing and arithmetic; drop the first and only two Rs remain

explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic; someone who cannot read is left with just two.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot read has lost the first of the traditional three basic skills, leaving only two.

clue.text: Mountains of fire seen rising

parts.note: a pyre is a pile of wood set on fire, as for a funeral

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so it is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Mountains where a blaze was seen climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round rather than suggesting the mountains climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The range along the border between France and Spain is a chain of mountains.

clue.text: A soul's untimely? Wrong if coming thus

definitions.text: A soul's untimely? Wrong if coming thus

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the preceding words are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soul arriving too early is at fault if it turns up together with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges A SOULS UNTIMELY; the clue as a whole says the arrival is mistimed if it happens all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening all at the same time, the very sense in which the arrivals would be badly timed.

clue.text: Coffee tins fashioned by worker

indicators.note: fashioned means made into a new shape, so the letters of tins are rearranged

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: A labourer makes up a batch of coffee tins.
explanation.walkthrough: Coffee tins suggests a container, but Coffee alone is the definition; the tins are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered coffee that dissolves straight away in hot water is the quick kind.

clue.text: Devious Greek character in debt in ship

indicators.note: the second in places that whole group inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: in means the Greek letter goes inside the word for debt

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgment of debt
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A shifty Greek is in debt aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek character looks like a person from Greece, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of winding turns, as a river or a twisting path is, the way a crooked argument winds about.

clue.text: Free simpleton to go round Kent?

indicators.note: to go round means the word for simpleton encircles the letters for the county's region

parts.note: a loon is a foolish or crazy person
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so it gives SE

explanation.surface: A fool is set free to wander about Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England, so it stands for SE, which LOON goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie or slacken a knot is to free it up, a verb sense matching loosen.

clue.text: Single-minded old boy's misused sieves

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, and the possessive adds an S

indicators.note: misused tells us the letters of sieves are put to a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A former pupil, obsessed with one thing, has been mishandling the kitchen strainers.
explanation.walkthrough: OB is old boy (a British term for a former pupil) and the 's gives S; 'misused' rearranges SIEVES to ESSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fixated on one thing is driven by a fixation, focused to excess.

clue.text: Suggest I'm to trade regularly

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to ply a trade or a route is to work at it regularly

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that they should go into business on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but it belongs to the definition of PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without saying it is to indicate it indirectly.

clue.text: Take steps to entertain Daniel before church

indicators.note: before says the short form of Daniel comes ahead of the church letters

parts.note: Dan is the short form of the name Daniel
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Arrangements are made for Daniel to perform before the church congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' is part of the surface: Dan entertains by dancing, but only 'Take steps' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in rhythm to music means stepping in a pattern, so the phrase is a playful synonym.

clue.text: Part of circle associated with a church

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, the church

explanation.surface: A section of a ring is linked to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved section of the circumference of a circle is the geometric term.

clue.text: Shortly has work brought in specified as "shell-shaped"

parts.note: has shortened is the contraction 's, giving S

indicators.note: brought in means the work abbreviation is inserted into the word for specified as

parts.note: called means named or specified as
op is the abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A designer briefly has a commission that is described as shaped like a seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly has' means the word has shortened to its contraction, an apostrophe and S, which supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge cut into a series of curves resembles the ridged rim of a mollusc's shell.

clue.text: Run off with energy and long stride

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a lope is a long easy bounding stride

explanation.surface: A runner bolts with vigour and a long, loping gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off to marry secretly are said to do this.

clue.text: Feature of bonnet trimmed after deductions

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A decorated hat is shown off, with its price given after discounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A net amount is what remains once tax and costs have been subtracted.

clue.text: Reaction of spa hotel is sly, evasive

parts.note: a hydro is a British hotel offering spa water treatments

indicators.note: evasive suggests dodging about, so the letters of is sly shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A spa hotel responds slyly and evasively to complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British spa hotel; 'evasive' rearranges IS SLY to LYSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting a compound by water is a chemical reaction, the general term here.
